Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the first innings of India Women! The players are making their way out in the middle now. Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma are the two openers for India Women. Lauren Cheatle on debut has the new ball in hand. Let's play...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

Australia Women got off to the worst possible start as a huge mix-up between the openers cost Phoebe Litchfield her wicket as she went back for a diamond duck. Ellyse Perry also perished soon after. Beth Mooney and Tahlia McGrath steadied things for the visitors with an 80-run stand before the latter got dismissed right after reaching her fifty. Mooney continued nicely but fell on the last delivery before Lunch which put the Aussies further on the back foot. There were some decent contributions from Alyssa Healy and Annabel Sutherland and the lower order chipped in with some as well, especially the last-wicket partnership between Lauren Cheatle and Kim Garth helped them get past the 200-run mark with the latter remaining unbeaten 28 off 71 balls. Now, it will be up to their bowlers to stop the Women in Blue to take a big lead in this game. Join us in a bit for India Women's reply.

India Women have put on another brilliant bowling performance here to bowl the Aussies out for 219! They picked up from where they left off against the England Women. The hosts were gifted the first wicket but a ripper of a delivery from Pooja Vastrakar to get rid of Ellyse Perry set the tone for them. The spinners were excellent as usual keeping the runs in check and picking up wickets at regular intervals as well. However, Pooja was the pick of the bowlers with four wickets while Sneh got three and Deepti Sharma ended with a couple. Things could have been even better if Deepti managed to hold on to those three chances and if they had taken a review of Beth Mooney. Ideally, they would have hoped to restrict the Aussies under 200, but will still be very happy.

SESSION SUMMARY - 77 runs and 4 wickets in 31 overs! Another really good session for the hosts! They have the Aussies in all sorts and the star for them have been Pooja Vastrakar and Deepti Sharma! For Australia Women, a couple of batters got off to starts but none went on to make it big. Tahlia McGrath was looking good but she fell right after reaching her fifty. It was the partnership between her and Beth Mooney that got them out of a troubling situation when they lost Phoebe Litchfield for a diamond duck and Ellyse Perry too. They are in a spot of bother at the moment and need a good partnership. Still a lot of batting to come and they would hope, the second session goes their way. Will we see a fightback? Join us at 12.10 pm (6.40 am GMT) to find out.

SESSION SUMMARY - 103 runs and 4 wickets in 29 overs! That wicket of Beth Mooney right before Lunch means this session belongs to the Indians. They have managed to get four wickets and not let the Aussies score freely too. It could have been a lot better though had they hung onto their chances but they will still be very pleased with their work. Deepti Sharma dropped Tahlia McGrath twice while the hosts did not take review when Beth Mooney was out. India will know though, that Australia bats deep and they need to continue to pick wickets. For now, though, they'll enter the break on top.

OUT! TAKEN! What a way to head into Lunch for India Women! Pooja Vastrakar strikes on the very last delivery in this session to remove Beth Mooney here. She bangs this one short and around off, angles in sharply, Beth Mooney hops up to fend it away but gets cramped up by the extra bounce and inward movement and the ball goes off the outside edge towards first slip where Sneh Rana makes no mistake. THAT WILL BE LUNCH ON DAY 1!

PITCH REPORT - Rohan Gavaskar is pitchside. He says that there is a buzz around and the conditions are a bit overcast. Adds that there is some moisture which will dry out. Tells spin will play a part but early on there will be some swing as well. She expects plenty of runs in this game.

On the other hand, this match and the series will officially mark the start of full-time captaincy for Alyssa Healy who is no stranger to leading the side but would have big shoes to fill in the sense of replacing Meg Lanning. This Australian team return to the longer format of the game after a special victory against England Women retaining the Ashes. The class all-rounders in the squad, with three or four of their potential top seven batters being exceptional bowlers make this team a powerhouse. Will Australia Women continue their domination over the hosts? Or will the Women in Blue write their names in the history books? We will find out soon. Toss and team news in a bit.

Harmanpreet Kaur and her team will be high on confidence with a massive victory under the belt against a tough English team not too long ago. The display of a complete team performance tossed with character and discipline resulted in a mammoth 347-run victory which Team India will look to carry forward into this game. India Women are yet to win a Test match against the Aussies who lead with 4 wins and 6 draws across 10 meetings. This match seems to be an ideal setting for the hosts to outperform themselves and get off the mark with the 'Win' against their names on the record books.
